column1: # Weighted benchmark scorecard: an additional view, never the ranking. Weights sum to 100. Thresholds are in the unit column.
# Higher-better: value >= threshold; lower-better: value <= threshold. status: proposed (changeable default) or fixed (stated definition).

column14: Excellent >= 99.9%, Good 99-99.89%, Moderate 95-98.99%, Poor below (the stated example definition); aligned-column weighted mean over samples.
Mirrors identity: 0.1 mismatches per 100 columns is the 99.9% identity line, 2.0 is roughly the 98% line.
Indels break reading frames, so the bands are set tighter than for substitutions only at the top.

No bands are defined: this metric needs a truth variant set that the benchmark does not yet carry, and the bands should be set by the panel once real values exist. Shown as not available and excluded from the overall.
Share of truth plasmid bases recovered; 0.99 leaves room for assembly gaps in repeats.
Share of truth plasmids recovered to at least 90% of their length.
Share of truth plasmids recovered at all, each plasmid weighted equally.
Conserved gene order from alignments (NGOC), else collinear fraction; it is not read- or graph-validated.

No bands are defined: this metric needs a truth variant set that the benchmark does not yet carry, and the bands should be set by the panel once real values exist. Shown as not available and excluded from the overall.
Share of circular truth plasmids recovered as one complete circular record; hard for short reads, hence lenient bands.
Mean completeness of repeat-rich truth plasmids, where collapsed or split repeats show up.
Resistance genes are the clinically actionable cargo, so the top bands are strict.
Share of truth proteins whose predicted CDS projects onto them at projection fraction >= 0.9; coordinates only.
Mean covered fraction of replicon, mobility and AMR elements on the truth plasmids.
Hardware-dependent: compare only runs made on the same machine and thread count.
2 GB fits a laptop, 8 GB a workstation, 32 GB a small server.
Share of isolates on which the tool ran to completion.
